description: Run the preflight analysis the settings of a session call for (what the Start button does) and return the plan to review, or nothing when the session should simply start. Use when: you start a session whose project has preflight on and want the same gate as the GUI. Not for: analysing an ad-hoc task (use run_preflight) or starting the session (use start_session). Returns: needed and, when true, the plan including its plan_id. Side effects: may run an analysis session that spends tokens; the project is not changed. Access: operate. Example: {"session_id":"lumen/P1"}

description: Switch a session's model, live if it is running. Use when: a task needs a stronger or cheaper model than the session currently uses. Not for: starting a session (use start_session with model) or changing the CLI (use set_session_runtime). Returns: ok and the session_id. Side effects: a running session is restarted on the new model with its conversation resumed; the choice is remembered as the session's default. Access: operate. Example: {"session_id":"lumen/P1","model":"sonnet"}

model.description: Model to switch to, e.g. opus or sonnet

session_id.description: Session ID in project/session form, e.g. lumen/P1; list them with get_sessions

title: Switch session model

description: Choose which agent CLI (claude or hermes) a session drives. Use when: a stopped session should run on another CLI the next time it starts. Not for: a running session (stop_session first) or changing the model (use set_session_model). Returns: ok and the session_id. Side effects: rewrites the session's runtime in the saved configuration; refused while the session runs. Access: operate. Example: {"session_id":"lumen/P1","runtime":"hermes"}

session_id.description: Session ID in project/session form, e.g. lumen/P1; list them with get_sessions

description: Turn the skill autopilot on or off for a project and set its daily budget. Use when: you are authorised to let the experience layer distil, trial and judge skills on its own. Not for: a single manual step (use distill_skill and approve_skill) or running one step now (use run_skill_autopilot). Returns: ok and the state and budget now in force. Side effects: writes the project's private config.local.toml; turning it on also turns on [optimization] experience_tracking, and the autopilot then spends tokens and writes skills into the project. Access: admin. Example: {"project":"lumen","enabled":true,"daily_budget_usd":2}

description: Replace the whole application config with an edited copy of what get_config returned. Use when: an edit needs fields the point tools do not reach, such as executable paths or workers. Not for: ordinary edits (use update_project, update_session or update_global_settings). Returns: the new config version; refused when the config changed since the version you pass. Side effects: rewrites the saved configuration and the project's .claude-manager folder; the GUI shows it after its next reload. Whatever you leave out is removed. Access: admin. annotations.title: Wait for any session to need a human

description: Block until the first of several sessions needs a human (question, permission, plan, error, finished task or turn), or the timeout passes. Use when: you operate several sessions and want one loop without polling: wait, handle what came, wait again. Not for: one specific status or event (use wait_for_status or wait_for_event). Returns: the first attention event with its session id in data.id; something already pending counts at once; on timeout reached=false with every session's status, not an error. Side effects: none, read only. Access: read. Example: {"session_ids":["lumen/P1","lumen/P2"],"timeout_ms":60000}

session_ids.description: Sessions to watch, each in project/session form, e.g. ["lumen/P1","lumen/P2"]

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait, in milliseconds (default 60000, at most 600000)

name: wait_for_any

current_status.description: Status of the awaited session right now (when not reached)

event.description: Name of the event that matched (when reached)

hint.description: What to do next (when not reached)

reached.description: True when the awaited event arrived; false when the wait timed out (not an error)

statuses.description: Status of every awaited session right now (when not reached)

timeout_ms.description: How long the wait lasted (when not reached)

title: Wait for any session to need a human

description: Block until an event whose payload contains the given fields is emitted, or the timeout passes. Use when: you wait for something other than a status, such as session:log or session:permission. Not for: session status changes (use wait_for_status). Returns: the matching event; recent past events count, so a short gap does not lose it; on timeout reached=false with a hint, not an error. Side effects: none, read only. Access: read. Example: {"event":"session:permission","match":{"id":"lumen/P1"}}

event.description: Event name, e.g. session:status, session:log, session:permission

match.description: Fields the event payload must contain, all of them, e.g. {"id": "lumen/P1"}

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait, in milliseconds (default 5000, at most 600000)

Side effects: none, read only. Access: read. Example: {"session_id":"lumen/P1","status":"idle","timeout_ms":30000}

description: Block until a mixed-programming task reaches a terminal status, or the timeout passes. Use when: dispatch_mixed_task runs in another call, or has returned and you want its final event. Side effects: none, read only; a timeout is reported as reached=false, not an error. Access: read. Example: {"task_id":"lumen/parse-header/step-flash","status":"done"}
